engines.name: 3.0L turbo V6 plug-in hybrid (60 TFSI e)

issues.t: Air suspension sags and the compressor wears out
issues.sym: One corner or the whole car sits low after parking, a suspension warning light, the compressor running often or loudly, or a harsh, uneven ride.
issues.why: The air struts leak as their rubber ages, which overworks the compressor until it fails. Ride height sensors can fail too.
issues.next: Have the system checked for leaks before replacing the compressor, or the new one will fail too. Replacing leaking struts and the compressor together is often the lasting fix.

issues.t: Timing belt failure bends the valves
issues.sym: The engine suddenly quits and will not restart, sometimes after a ticking or squeal from the front of the engine.
issues.why: The 3.7L and 4.2L V8 engines in these years use a timing belt. Worn belts, tensioners or rollers can let it slip or break, and the engine's valves then hit the pistons.
issues.next: If there is no record of a belt, tensioner and roller change in the last 100,000 miles or so, have it done now. An independent Audi specialist or a dealer can do the job.

issues.t: Timing chain and tensioner wear on the 4.2 FSI
issues.sym: A rattle from the engine on cold start, then cam timing codes or rough running if it gets worse.
issues.why: The direct-injection 4.2L V8 has several timing chains with tensioners and guides that wear, usually from around 100,000 miles. The chains are at the back of the engine, so the repair is big.
issues.next: Do not ignore a startup rattle. Have the cam timing checked; on high-mileage cars, chains and guides are best replaced before they fail.

issues.t: MMI screen freezes, dims or won't boot
issues.sym: The MMI infotainment screen locks up, goes dim or black, the navigation will not load, the radio and settings stop responding, or on 2011-2018 cars the pop-up screen sticks and will not open or close.
issues.why: Early MMI units suffer hard drive and screen failures with age and need software updates; the later retractable screen's mechanism and software can also fail.
issues.next: Try a system reset and ask about software updates first. If hardware has failed, a used or rebuilt unit can be coded to the car.

issues.t: Oil leaks from valve cover and camshaft seals
issues.sym: Oil spots under the car, a burning-oil smell after a drive, oily residue on the engine, and the oil level falling between changes.
issues.why: Valve cover gaskets, camshaft seals and oil pan gaskets on these V8s harden with age. A clogged crankcase vent (PCV) can push oil past them faster.
issues.next: Have the leak traced and the gaskets replaced before oil drips onto the exhaust. Check the crankcase vent at the same time.

issues.t: Automatic transmission shifts harshly or slips
issues.sym: Harsh or delayed shifts, the engine revving between gears, lurching from a stop, or the car not wanting to engage a gear.
issues.why: Old or low fluid, leaks and internal wear of clutches and solenoids in the 5-speed automatic.
issues.next: Check for fluid leaks and have a transmission scan done. A fluid service or solenoid repair can help if caught early; slipping usually means a rebuild.

issues.t: Plastic coolant pipe at the oil filter housing leaks
issues.sym: A large coolant leak on the passenger side above the oil pan, a low coolant warning, and a sweet coolant smell.
issues.why: A plastic coolant union pipe on the oil filter housing of the 4.2L V8 cracks with age. The part is small, but reaching it means taking a lot of the engine apart.
issues.next: Keep an eye on the coolant level and stop if the engine overheats. Get quotes from an Audi specialist; aluminum replacement pipes are available.

issues.t: Carbon buildup on the intake valves
issues.sym: Rough idle, misfires and a gradual loss of power, sometimes with a check engine light.
issues.why: On direct-injection engines fuel never washes the intake valves, so oil vapor bakes onto them and restricts airflow, typically from about 60,000-80,000 miles.
issues.next: If misfires persist after coils and plugs, ask for the intake valves to be inspected and walnut-blasted.

issues.t: W12 burns oil and builds sludge
issues.sym: The oil level drops quickly between changes, blue smoke, or a low-oil warning.
issues.why: The 6.0L W12 uses a lot of oil and does not tolerate long oil change intervals. Sludge can block oil passages and speed up timing chain wear.
issues.next: Check the oil often and change it every 5,000-7,500 miles with the correct oil. Have the timing chains checked if you hear rattles.

issues.t: Control arm bushings and ball joints wear
issues.sym: Clunks over bumps, vague or wandering steering, and uneven tire wear.
issues.why: The many aluminum control arms in the front suspension have rubber bushings and ball joints that wear out, often around 60,000-80,000 miles.
issues.next: Have the front suspension checked for play and replace worn arms, then get an alignment.

issues.t: Brief rattle on cold start from the 3.0T
issues.sym: A rattle lasting 1-3 seconds from the back of the engine on the first cold start of the day.
issues.why: Audi traced it to an upper timing chain tensioner. Audi says it does not cause damage.
issues.next: Ask the dealer about bulletin 2039995, which installs improved tensioners on both sides.

issues.t: Coolant pump leaks and coolant level drops
issues.sym: A low coolant warning, coolant falling with no puddle under the car, a check engine light, sometimes a low-boost code (P0299).
issues.why: The coolant pump on the 3.0L V6 can leak, and coolant can contaminate a vacuum switch valve. A 2026 lawsuit says the pump wears out early and can lead to overheating.
issues.next: Have a pressure test done when the warning appears and do not drive if it overheats. Ask about Audi bulletin 2070349 while under warranty.

issues.t: Oil leaks from the cylinder head cover
issues.sym: Oil level dropping, a burning-oil smell, and oil residue around the valve covers or under the car.
issues.why: Audi found metal shavings left in the cylinder head cover sealing groove at the factory, causing leaks around the cover, injectors and valve-lift actuator.
issues.next: Have it resealed before oil reaches the hot exhaust, and mention Audi bulletin 2053278.

issues.t: Turbo oil strainer can clog and wreck the turbos (recall)
issues.sym: Turbo whine, loss of boost, the engine refusing to idle, or stalling.
issues.why: A blocked oil strainer on the 4.0L twin-turbo V8 starves the turbo bearings, which can break the turbo shaft. Owners report major turbo repairs before the recall.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. The dealer replaces the strainer and changes the oil free; if turbos already failed, ask about reimbursement.

issues.t: High-pressure fuel pump supply line can leak (recall)
issues.sym: A fuel smell from the engine bay.
issues.why: The fuel line feeding the high-pressure pump can become porous and leak, which is a fire risk. A second recall added a pressure damper.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and do not drive if you smell fuel.

issues.t: Fuel rails can leak (recall)
issues.sym: A fuel smell from the engine bay.
issues.why: The left and right fuel rails on the supercharged V6 can leak fuel, which is a fire risk.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. The dealer replaces both rails free.

issues.t: Engine bay seal can touch hot parts (recall)
issues.sym: A loose rubber seal at the edge of the hood or a burning-rubber smell.
issues.why: The engine compartment seal can come loose and rest on hot engine parts, which is a fire risk.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. The dealer fits a retaining plate free.

issues.t: Coolant valve can leak into the engine computer (recall)
issues.sym: Loss of power, stalling, or coolant loss.
issues.why: A leaking coolant valve can let coolant run into the engine control module connector.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. The dealer replaces the valve and checks the connector free.

issues.t: Sunroof glass may come loose (recall)
issues.sym: No warning before failure; the glass panel could separate while driving.
issues.why: The sunroof glass may not be properly bonded to its frame.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. The dealer adds adhesive between the glass and frame free.

issues.t: Sunroof glass can shatter (recall)
issues.sym: Cracks in the sunroof glass or the panel breaking.
issues.why: On cars built in mid-2013, the standard sunroof glass panel can shatter.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. The dealer replaces the glass free.

issues.t: Driver or passenger airbag may not work correctly (recall)
issues.sym: An airbag warning light, or no sign at all before a crash.
issues.why: On 2004-2005 cars the driver airbag may not unfold properly. On 2006-2007 cars a wiring issue or a weak battery can switch the passenger airbag off when it should be on.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. Dealers replace the airbag, modify the wiring or update the airbag computer free.

issues.t: Shifter can leave Park without the key (recall)
issues.sym: The gear lever can be moved out of Park without the key in the ignition, and the car could roll away.
issues.why: The automatic transmission's locking cable can shift out of position.
issues.next: Always set the parking brake. Check your VIN for open recalls; the dealer installs an adjusting piece free.

issues.t: Driver airbag can go off from static shock (recall)
issues.sym: In very dry weather, the driver airbag could deploy when the driver touches the steering wheel.
issues.why: Static electricity could trigger the airbag's firing circuit.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. The dealer installs a ground wire free.

issues.t: Driver airbag inflator can absorb moisture (recall)
issues.sym: No warning before a crash.
issues.why: Moisture can get into the driver airbag inflator, so it may burst or underinflate in a crash.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls right away and have the inflator replaced free.

issues.t: Fuel filler neck can leak fuel vapor (recall)
issues.sym: A fuel smell near the filler door.
issues.why: The filler neck's cover may not seal, letting fuel vapor escape.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. The dealer replaces the filler neck and expansion tank free.

issues.t: Moisture in engine computer connector can stall the engine (recall)
issues.sym: Warning lights, rough running, or the engine stalling.
issues.why: A missing sealing pin lets moisture into the engine control module connector.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Check your VIN for open recalls. The dealer installs the pin and replaces corroded connectors free.

issues.t: Rear trailing arm nut can break (recall)
issues.sym: The car pulls or tracks oddly, or the rear tires wear unevenly.
issues.why: The lock nut on a rear trailing arm can crack from stress corrosion and misalign the rear axle. A follow-up recall checks alignment on repaired cars.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. The dealer replaces the nuts and checks alignment free.

issues.t: Rear camera screen blank from infotainment fault (recall)
issues.sym: A black or blank screen instead of the camera image when reversing.
issues.why: Software errors, and on some cars damage inside the infotainment unit at shutoff, can stop the camera image from appearing.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. The dealer updates the software or replaces the unit free.

issues.t: Passenger airbag may deploy too forcefully (recall)
issues.sym: No warning before a crash.
issues.why: The front passenger airbag may be folded wrongly and inflate with too much force.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. The dealer replaces the airbag module free.

issues.t: Front passenger airbag may switch off (recall)
issues.sym: The passenger airbag 'off' light shows with an adult in the seat.
issues.why: A loose connection at the passenger occupant detection module can turn off the airbag.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. The dealer replaces the module free.

issues.t: Rear camera image may not display (recall)
issues.sym: The rear camera picture is missing or wrong when reversing.
issues.why: A software error can stop the rearview camera image from displaying.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. The dealer updates the software free.

issues.t: Water pump and thermostat housing leak coolant
issues.sym: Coolant level slowly dropping, a sweet smell after driving, pink or white crust on the front of the engine, or a low coolant warning.
issues.why: The plastic water pump and thermostat housing on the supercharged 3.0L V6 develop leaks, mostly on higher-mileage cars.
issues.next: Have the cooling system pressure tested. Replace the leaking pump or housing before the engine overheats.

issues.t: Sunroof drains clog and leak water inside
issues.sym: Damp carpets, water dripping from the headliner or pillars, or a musty smell after rain.
issues.why: The drain tubes at the corners of the sunroof tray clog with debris, so rainwater overflows into the cabin.
issues.next: Have the drains cleared and tested. Dry wet carpets quickly, since water can damage modules and wiring under them.

issues.t: Crankcase vent (PCV) valve fails
issues.sym: An oil smell, rough idle, whistling from the engine, or oil use between changes.
issues.why: The crankcase vent and oil separator on the supercharged V6 and twin-turbo V8 wear out with age.
issues.next: Have the PCV valve and oil separator checked if the engine idles rough or smells of oil; many owners replace it around 80,000 miles.
